supports: Textron is a real listed counterparty (CIK 0000217346)
Surf Air's filings provide detailed contract terms suggesting a real executed instrument
C-001.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (Textron CIK 0000217346 for 'Surf Air', 'Surf Air Mobility', 'SAM Aircraft', 'SAM System')
C-001.M_value: 0 hits across all four search terms in Textron's SEC filings as of 2024-06-30
C-001.interpretation: Textron has not disclosed Surf Air as a counterparty in any SEC filing. With ~$400M+ aggregate purchase commitments, this is notable but not dispositive — Textron is a $13B revenue conglomerate so Surf Air is immaterial to them. The contract is real (filed as 10-K exhibit) but the counterparty's silence indicates Surf Air is not strategically meaningful to Textron. Per heuristic 4 (investment partners often don't disclose) and heuristic 7 (PASS or MODERATE on 0 disclosure absent strong materiality threshold), MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: contract exists but the 'strategic partnership' framing oversells Textron's commitment.

supports: Stock-for-services payment to Palantir is a strong indicator the relationship is at least functionally underway
C-002.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (Palantir CIK 0001321655 for 'Surf Air' and 'Surf Air Mobility')
C-002.M_value: 0 hits in Palantir's SEC filings as of 2024-06-30
C-002.interpretation: Palantir has not disclosed Surf Air as a customer. Palantir does not normally name individual commercial customers in 10-Ks, so absence is consistent with normal disclosure. The fact that SRFM had to settle $2M in payables to Palantir with stock (rather than cash) is a financial-distress signal but does not contradict the partnership. The aggregate $50M/7-yr commitment ($7.1M/yr) is the largest single fixed cost on SRFM's books — worth flagging that a going-concern company is committed to it. MODERATE: real relationship, but stock-for-service payment is a soft red flag indicating SRFM cannot fund the contract.

supports: Jetstream is referenced in 7 SEC filings (mostly SRFM's own + the Tuscan SPAC predecessor)
C-003.M_value: 7 hits, but all from SRFM/Tuscan filings — no independent third-party reference
C-003.interpretation: The filing itself self-discloses the contradiction: '$450M aircraft purchase / leaseback ... No transactions have been executed under this agreement as of December 31, 2023.' Signed October 2022 — 14+ months elapsed without a single executed transaction. With a $120M minimum usage obligation, zero usage means SRFM is on a path toward a contract liability or termination. This is RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE: management headlines a $450M financing facility while the body of the filing concedes 0% of it has been used. Direct contradiction between marketing-tier disclosure and operational reality.

supports: The development pathway (STC under FAA) is regulated and verifiable as a process; the partnership with TAI provides licensing scaffolding
C-005.M_value: 0 patent applications and 0 granted patents under either name, in any technology bucket (electric_powertrain, aircraft, other)
C-005.interpretation: ZERO patent footprint as of cutoff for a company claiming to be developing a novel hybrid-electric powertrain product targeting FAA STC certification in early 2027. By comparison, even early-stage eVTOL/electric-aviation peers typically have 5-50+ patent applications by the time they have publicly announced a 3-year-out cert milestone. The IP is presumably owned by partners (TAI license is non-exclusive into existing TAI IP) — meaning the SAM System's underlying IP belongs to others, not SRFM. This contradicts the framing of SRFM as the technology developer. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE per Nikola pattern: zero granted patents in claimed core technology areas.
